quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (the first after absorbing HD Hyundai Infracore by merger on 2026-01-01; the filing states the acquired construction-equipment and engine businesses are reflected from that date): consolidated Q2 2026 revenue of KRW 2,434,171 million against KRW 967,708 million in Q2 2025, Q2 operating profit of KRW 248,883,827 thousand (Q2 2025: KRW 40,043,555 thousand) and Q2 net income of KRW 180,694,612 thousand (Q2 2025: KRW 620,645 thousand). H1 2026 revenue was KRW 4,739,038 million (H1 2025: KRW 1,874,547 million), operating profit KRW 439,582 million (H1 2025: KRW 81,694 million) and net income KRW 354,565 million (H1 2025: KRW 26,272 million). Consolidated subsidiaries rose to 25 from 10 at the start of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue KRW 2,434,171 million (Q2 2025: KRW 967,708 million); Q2 operating profit KRW 248,883,827 thousand (Q2 2025: KRW 40,043,555 thousand); H1 revenue KRW 4,739,038 million, H1 operating profit KRW 439,582 million

quarterly_data.signal: Segments and product mix, H1 2026: the construction equipment segment had revenue of KRW 5,761,351 million (including KRW 1,614,337 million of inter-segment sales) and operating profit of KRW 355,522 million; the engine segment, added with the HD Hyundai Infracore merger, had revenue of KRW 743,365 million (including KRW 151,341 million inter-segment), operating profit of KRW 84,060 million and net income of KRW 73,593 million. External sales by product: construction equipment KRW 3,572,942 million (75.40%), industrial vehicles KRW 200,508 million (4.23%), parts and other KRW 373,564 million (7.88%), engines and engine A/S parts for industrial and generator use KRW 592,024 million (12.49%). Exports were KRW 4,041,942 million and domestic sales KRW 697,096 million (exports about 85.3%). Revenue from contracts with customers by region: Korea KRW 684,207 million, North America KRW 830,747 million, Asia including the Middle East KRW 961,008 million, Europe KRW 970,890 million, other countries KRW 1,328,544 million. No customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated revenue. Average domestic selling prices: wheel excavator KRW 168 million, 20-ton excavator KRW 169 million, 30-ton excavator KRW 206 million.
quarterly_data.figure: engine segment revenue KRW 743,365 million, operating profit KRW 84,060 million; construction equipment segment operating profit KRW 355,522 million; exports about 85.3% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Engine business: engines are sold in Korea directly, through dealers and in-house, and exported through dealers and leading overseas OEMs. Small engines entered the market by being fitted to Doosan Bobcat equipment and the company keeps adding outside customers such as forklift and agricultural-machinery makers; medium and large engines serve vehicle makers with solutions for the latest emission rules and generator and marine makers with a broad line-up. The company says it is expanding supply of eco-friendly engines that meet the latest emission regulations to existing customers and to domestic and overseas generator and industrial-equipment makers, pursuing demand for EU Stage V engines, and building a new Gunsan plant to make new product families. Company outlook (filing): it expects growth opportunities from emission-rule transitions, the growing high-output large-engine market and emerging-market demand, and sees an opportunity in rising demand for internal-combustion engines as prime and backup power as AI-driven power demand centred on data centers grows; it notes that generator-engine demand is affected by the expansion and up-sizing of data centers. H1 2026 engine capacity was 73,966 units at the parent (50,938 produced, 68.87% utilisation) and 4,060 units at HD Construction Equipment (Tianjin) Engine (3,917 produced, 96.48%); the average domestic price was KRW 24 million for a generator engine and KRW 6 million for an industrial engine.
quarterly_data.figure: engine capacity 73,966 units at the parent (68.87% utilisation); generator engine average price KRW 24 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and utilisation, H1 2026 (combined group after the merger): total capacity of 119,210 units against production of 78,685 units, an average utilisation of 66.01% (FY2025, before the merger: capacity 50,140, production 20,202). Construction equipment: parent capacity 24,510 units with 12,847 produced (52.42%); India 4,500 / 4,354 (96.76%); Brazil 2,000 / 715 (35.75%); HD Construction Equipment (China) 9,580 / 5,338 (55.72%); Norway articulated dump trucks 200 / 182 (91.00%). The Jiangsu excavator subsidiary stopped production in April 2025 and its 394 units are OEM volume; the parent's capacity may shift until the Ulsan campus upgrade project stabilises.

Order book: on 2026-01-28 the company signed an engine supply contract with Hyundai Rotem to supply part of the second batch of engines for the K2 tanks Hyundai Rotem builds for export to Poland (contract term 2026-01-27 to 2027-12-31; the amount is withheld from disclosure). The company does not disclose quantities, amounts, delivered amounts or order backlog, citing trade secrets.
The engine supply contract for Turkey's next-generation tank with BMC Otomotiv Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S., signed 2023-02-01, worth KRW 110,200,000,000 and running to 2028-02-28, is still in progress.
quarterly_data.counterparty: BMC Otomotiv Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Investment: H1 2026 additions to property, plant and equipment were KRW 124,519 million, and construction in progress (mainly the new Gunsan ultra-large and defence engine plant) carried acquisition commitments of KRW 120,790 million. Ongoing projects: construction-equipment plant extension (Jan 2022 to Jul 2026, KRW 207,230 million, KRW 207,138 million invested), new-model dies and jigs (2026, KRW 134,749 million, KRW 29,593 million invested) and an engine plant extension (Jan 2023 to Dec 2026, KRW 130,587 million, KRW 83,296 million invested, KRW 47,291 million still to invest). Planned investment totals KRW 868,646 million: KRW 339,553 million in 2026, KRW 263,168 million in 2027 and KRW 265,925 million in 2028, of which the engine plant extension and tooling is KRW 266,694 million (KRW 130,587 million in 2026, KRW 57,426 million in 2027, KRW 78,681 million in 2028); the company says the yearly amounts may be adjusted to business conditions.
quarterly_data.figure: planned investment KRW 868,646 million for 2026 to 2028 (engine plant extension KRW 266,694 million); Gunsan engine plant commitments KRW 120,790 million

quarterly_data.signal: Purchasing, H1 2026: main raw-material purchases (including intra-group) totalled KRW 2,459,119 million, of which engine parts bought by the parent were KRW 437,219 million (17.78%) and by the Tianjin engine plant KRW 17,735 million. Named main suppliers: excavator parts from Oseong Gigong and Seonjin Jeonggong (romanised), wheel-loader parts from ZF Friedrichshafen AG (supply described as highly concentrated) and engine parts from Cascode (romanised; the company holds 19.35% of it). Representative purchase prices: excavator bucket assembly KRW 1,900 thousand, wheel-loader main control valve EUR 1,224, engine injector assembly EUR 49.6. Related-party purchases of goods included KRW 266,711 million from parent HD Hyundai Site Solution, KRW 72,263 million from HD Hyundai Hydraulic Machinery (Changzhou) and KRW 16,867 million from HD Hyundai Oilbank.
quarterly_data.figure: raw-material purchases KRW 2,459,119 million; engine parts KRW 437,219 million (17.78%)

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: H1 2026 R&D spending was KRW 143,506 million (3.48% of revenue). Listed projects include new construction-equipment models for regional emission rules, electric-excavator integrated control and mini electric-excavator efficiency, engines for European emission regulations, diesel / gas engines and eco-friendly hydrogen engines for industrial and commercial vehicles, and battery packs for industrial and commercial vehicles. Intellectual property at 30 June 2026: 1,737 patents, 359 designs and 440 trademarks.

Market position and strategy (filing): the company puts its 2025 global construction-equipment market share, combined with the former HD Hyundai Infracore, at about 2.3%, against Caterpillar 15.2%, Komatsu 11.0%, XCMG 5.8% and John Deere 5.4% (Yellow Table, by sales). It merged with HD Hyundai Infracore to complement the product portfolio, streamline operations, strengthen global competitiveness and create brand and sales-channel synergies; it aims to cement its No. 1 share in Korea with new models and service, pursue profitability-led growth in China, and raise share in North America and Europe with next-generation products, wider channel coverage and key-account sales.
